description: Behavioral cases for know-thyself, written from prompts users really type. Run each in a fresh session against a frozen corpus copy, then run evals/grade.py on the reply and report for the yes-or-no checks, and judge the rest pairwise as evals/JUDGE.md describes.

cases.expect: A description of how the user works, with counts and short dated quotes, and no advice. It ends with three to five follow-ups the user could paste, written from what this run found.

cases.prompt: how do I work with agents?
cases.expect: Same as run: a mirror, not coaching, ending with tailored follow-ups.

cases.prompt: coach me on how I start tasks
cases.expect: Coaching scoped to how the user opens tasks: at most three habit cards that bear on it, a few next steps with a short why each, and one annotated Sources section at the end with at most five entries. No inline links in the body.

cases.prompt: has splitting work across agents changed since August?
cases.expect: Answers whether the habit changed, with counts on both sides and the verdict the script gives, after ruling out a shift in tools or projects. No coaching unless asked.

cases.prompt: what did I decide about how to handle flaky tests?
cases.expect: What was decided, when, and where (source, session, timestamp), the latest decision first when they conflict. No coaching.
